label: New daycare or preschool

what_happens.title: What happens at daycare
goals: Daycare is a place to play and learn with other kids
The day has a shape: play, snack, outside, nap, stories
A grown-up always comes back at pick-up
what_happens.parentSkill: Describe the day in order using activities, not times: play, snack, outside, nap, pick-up.

who_is_there.title: Who is at daycare
goals: Teachers look after the children and keep them safe
Teachers help with toilets, food and feelings
who_is_there.parentSkill: Learn the teacher's name and say it at home: "Tomorrow Miss Ana will say hello."

what_i_do.title: What I do at daycare
goals: Hang the bag, say hello, do the goodbye ritual
Ask for help with toilets, food and feelings
what_i_do.parentSkill: Create a short goodbye ritual (hug, kiss, wave at the window) and use it every day.

if_scared.title: If I miss home
goals: Crying is okay, and teachers help
Calm tools: heart on the hand, a photo, slow breaths
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling at drop-off: 'You'll miss me. I'll be back after nap.' Then leave calmly.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise daycare
goals: Play daycare with toys at home
rehearsal.parentSkill: Play daycare: toys are kids, your child is the teacher, and you practise goodbyes and pick-ups.

steps: Walk to daycare with a grown-up and a bag
Hang the bag and coat on my own hook
Say good morning to the teacher
Do the goodbye ritual and wave at the window
Play, have snack, go outside and have nap or quiet time
Sing songs and read stories in circle time
Pick-up time: a grown-up comes back
sensory: lots of children talking and laughing
bright toys and paintings on the walls
the smell of snack and crayons
a little cot or mat for nap time
a new hook with my name or picture
a squishy feeling in the tummy at goodbye
honestyNotes: Goodbyes can be hard and crying is common for the first days or weeks; never sneak away and never promise the child will not miss the parent. Always say when the grown-up comes back using the daily routine (after nap, after snack), not clock times.

fallbackAnswer: Yes. [[GROWNUP]] always comes back at pick-up time.
Pick-up is after nap, or after afternoon snack.
Missing [[GROWNUP]] is normal. You can press the heart on your hand.
A teacher can give you a cuddle too.
A teacher is a grown-up whose job is looking after kids.
They will say good morning and learn your name.

questionButtons.text: What if I need the toilet?
fallbackAnswer: Tell the teacher, I need the toilet. Teachers help with that every day.
It is good to ask.
There are lots of kids, and some are new too.
You can play next to someone, or say, can I play?

questionButtons.text: Do I have to sleep there?
fallbackAnswer: There is a nap or quiet time on a little bed or mat.
You can bring your blanket from home, and resting is fine even without sleep.
Crying is okay. Lots of kids cry at goodbye.
Teachers know how to help, and feelings get smaller.
There is snack time, and maybe lunch.
You can say no thank you, and eat what you like.

questionButtons.text: What if it is too loud?
fallbackAnswer: Daycare can be loud when everyone plays.
You can rest in a quiet corner or tell the teacher.

questionButtons.text: What will I do all day?
fallbackAnswer: Play, snack, outside time, nap and stories.
Then [[GROWNUP]] comes back.

techniques.label: A goodbye ritual
techniques.how: Do the same short goodbye every day: hug, kiss, wave at the window.

techniques.label: A heart on the hand
techniques.how: Draw matching hearts on your hands to press when missing each other.

techniques.label: A family photo
techniques.how: Put a small family photo in the bag or cubby.

techniques.label: Picture schedule
techniques.how: Draw the day in pictures: play, snack, outside, nap, pick-up.

techniques.label: Visiting first
techniques.how: Visit the room, the hook and the toilets before the first day.

techniques.label: A comfort blanket or toy
techniques.how: Pack a small blanket or toy for nap time.

techniques.label: Asking the teacher
techniques.how: Practise the sentence, can you help me, please?

techniques.label: A quiet corner
techniques.how: Ask the teacher where the quiet corner is for a rest.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Hang my bag on my hook
Hug, kiss, wave at the window

pain: If you get a bump, the teacher will help.
Tell a teacher if something hurts.
body: Tell the teacher when you need the toilet.
You can eat what you like at snack.
sensory: Daycare can be loud. The quiet corner helps.
strangers: The teacher's job is to look after you. Let's say good morning.
You can ask, can you help me, please?
separation: I'll be back after nap. I always come back.
Press the heart on your hand when you miss me.
unknown: Play, snack, outside, nap, then pick-up.
First hang your bag, then we say goodbye.
safety: If you are not sure, ask a teacher.
social: You can play next to someone first.
love: I love you, and I think of you all day.
I'm proud of you for trying.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] will start daycare.
Daycare is a place where kids play, learn and have fun while grown-ups are at work.
First [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] walk in together.
Then [[CHILD]] hangs the bag on a hook with a name or a picture.
Before bed, here is a story about a little duckling called Dot.
Dot was starting at the Pond Daycare.
First Mama Duck walked Dot to the big willow tree.
Then Dot found a little hook with a picture of a leaf.
That is your hook, said the kind goose teacher.
Next Dot played with pebbles and floating leaves.
After that there was snack time, with crunchy seeds.
Then the ducklings had a nap in soft reeds.
When Dot woke up, there was a song about raindrops.
And then, Mama Duck came back, just as she said.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
Next there is play time with blocks, paint and books.
After that comes snack, outside time, and nap or quiet time.
There are songs and stories in circle time.
Last, at pick-up time, [[GROWNUP]] comes back.
[[CHILD]] can remember the day like a song: play, snack, outside, nap, pick-up.

At daycare there are teachers whose job is to look after children.
They keep kids safe, help with toilets, snack and coats, and give cuddles when kids are sad.
There are other kids too, and some of them are new.
Some kids feel shy, and some feel excited.
In the story, Dot the duckling met the goose teacher, Miss Feather.
Miss Feather had soft grey wings and a warm voice.
Good morning, Dot, she said.
Dot hid behind Mama's wing a little.
Then Dot saw a frog called Fin, sitting alone by the water.
Fin was new too.
Dot and Fin played with pebbles side by side, without talking.
Later, Fin said, want to splash?
Dot nodded, and they splashed together.
When Dot felt sad, Miss Feather gave her a soft wing hug.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
The teacher will say good morning and learn [[CHILD]]'s name.
Friends take a little time to make.
Playing side by side is a great start.
Teachers can help kids find a game together.

Daycare has a daily rhythm that repeats, so after a week [[CHILD]] will know what comes next.
Teachers plan activities that help kids grow, like painting, building and sharing.
Nap time lets small bodies rest so the afternoon is fun too.
[[GROWNUP]] gets a report about the day and can talk about it at home.
[[CHILD]] can ask for a picture schedule of the day.
Daycare teachers are trained in child safety and first aid, and they know every child in the room.
Some children cry at drop-off for a few days, and teachers know how to comfort them.
Kids this age often play side by side before they play together, which is how friendships start.
[[GROWNUP]] can share [[CHILD]]'s comfort tips with the teacher.
[[CHILD]] can bring a family photo to look at during the day.
A short, cheerful goodbye is easier than a long one, even if there are tears.
Kids who know the plan for the day settle faster.
Joining in can start small: handing someone a block or sitting near a group.
Telling a teacher about hunger, thirst or the toilet is a big kid skill.
[[CHILD]] can choose one thing to try each day.
Missing a parent is a sign of a strong bond, not a problem.
The first two weeks are usually the hardest, and most kids settle after that.
Tiredness and hunger can make feelings bigger, so rest and snack help.
If [[CHILD]] has a hard day, telling [[GROWNUP]] at home helps the teacher help more.
[[CHILD]] can choose a small comfort item for the bag.
Visiting the daycare before the first day helps a lot: seeing the room, the hook and the toilets.
Reading a book about daycare together makes the day familiar.
Practising short separations, like a grandparent visit, builds confidence.
A pick-up treat ritual gives something to look forward to.
[[CHILD]] can pack the bag the night before.
